name: Business and Management Autonomous Research Benchmark (BMA-ARB)
evidence_note: Twelve anchor tasks and twelve counterfactual variants spanning computational, synthesis and secondary-data production systems. The public headline remains raw autonomous task pass rate.
claim_boundary: Design-complete but not directly scored. It measures technically complete, verifiable papers and does not itself predict journal acceptance.

name: Portsmouth Business School Research Production Frontier
evidence_note: Planned extension of BMA-ARB. It will estimate journal-ready outputs, resource cost, released academic capacity and the lowest-cost compute and verification portfolio, weighted to Portsmouth's observed output portfolio.
claim_boundary: No production-function estimate exists until Portsmouth task demand, human effort and direct benchmark runs are observed. Zero owned GPUs remains an admissible recommendation.

name: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
evidence_note: An early end-to-end paper-generation system covering idea generation, coding, experiments, manuscript production and automated review.
claim_boundary: Focused on machine-learning experiments; automated review is not an independent journal-quality assessment.

name: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
evidence_note: Extends the original AI Scientist with agentic tree search and reports a fully AI-generated paper accepted at a workshop.
claim_boundary: Workshop acceptance in machine learning does not establish repeatable journal readiness across business and management.

name: CORE-Bench
evidence_note: A reproducibility benchmark built from published research artefacts, with 270 tasks from 90 papers across three disciplines.
claim_boundary: Reproduces supplied studies rather than producing a new journal article from an open research brief.

name: PaperBench
evidence_note: Evaluates agents asked to replicate 20 ICML papers using detailed paper-specific criteria.
claim_boundary: Replication of machine-learning papers is narrower than autonomous business-research production.

name: AIRA-dojo
evidence_note: An evolutionary research-agent scaffold that searches over candidate machine-learning solutions.
claim_boundary: Optimises machine-learning task metrics rather than complete journal outputs.

name: AIRS-Bench
evidence_note: Twenty machine-learning research tasks derived from frontier papers, evaluated over a full experimental lifecycle without baseline code.
claim_boundary: Task metrics and machine-learning artefacts do not establish journal-ready business research.

name: AIRA2
evidence_note: Addresses evaluation and execution bottlenecks in machine-learning research agents using asynchronous multi-GPU search and hidden-consistent evaluation.
claim_boundary: Evidence concerns machine-learning benchmark performance under large accelerator budgets.

name: MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research
evidence_note: Uses budget-aware Monte Carlo tree search, modular solution construction and comparative reflective memory.
claim_boundary: The search policy is transferable; reported evidence remains within machine-learning research tasks.

name: FIRE-Bench
evidence_note: Evaluates constrained rediscovery from research papers and code, scoring claims as well as execution across staged research workflows.
claim_boundary: Constrained rediscovery is not equivalent to choosing a novel business-research question or meeting a journal standard.

name: ReplicatorBench
evidence_note: Evaluates end-to-end replication in social and behavioural science, including claim extraction, data retrieval and analysis.
claim_boundary: Replication capability does not directly estimate the resource cost of producing a new journal-ready paper.

name: SocSci-Repro-Bench
evidence_note: A 221-task benchmark across four social-science disciplines and thirteen domains; it also examines confirmatory specification search induced by prompt framing.
claim_boundary: Reproduction with original materials is a component of production, not a full research production function.

name: Project APE
evidence_note: A live programme that generated 1,000 autonomous empirical policy-evaluation papers with public data, code, papers and failures, followed by automated review and revision.
claim_boundary: Its tournament is a triage mechanism, not peer review, and does not estimate total human-compute cost per journal-ready output.

name: CRED: Cost-Recall Evaluation of Defect Detectors
evidence_note: A living benchmark of AI research verifiers using known injected defects, deterministic matching and human adjudication, with explicit recall-cost frontiers.
claim_boundary: Defect recall is not a journal-readiness measure; multiple-error performance and false-finding control remain material.

name: HeurekaBench
evidence_note: A framework for benchmarking AI co-scientists on open-ended questions grounded in experimental data, papers and code.
claim_boundary: It evaluates scientific analysis, not institution-level output cost or an observed journal portfolio.

name: PhysGym
evidence_note: An interactive physics-discovery environment with controlled priors, designed to test rule learning through experimentation.
claim_boundary: Synthetic physics worlds provide exact rules but omit many ambiguities of organisational data.

name: DiscoverPhysics
evidence_note: Tests agents in 22 counterfactual physical worlds and separates predictive success from correct explanation.
claim_boundary: Results concern simulated physical discovery rather than business-research production.

name: AutoResearchBench
evidence_note: Evaluates deep and wide research discovery from literature, with frontier systems remaining weak on the full benchmark.
claim_boundary: Focuses on discovery and planning rather than executable articles and resource cost.

name: AutoResearchClaw
evidence_note: Combines multi-agent debate, execution repair and seven human-intervention modes; reported results favour focused intervention over both full autonomy and exhaustive oversight.
claim_boundary: Its intervention findings need replication in business and management tasks with academic time priced explicitly.

name: ResearchClawBench
evidence_note: Forty paper-grounded tasks across ten domains; reported failures concentrate in protocol fidelity, evidence integration and scientific core work.
claim_boundary: Task scores do not equal journal readiness or whole-school research productivity.

name: NatureBench
evidence_note: Ninety tasks drawn from Nature-family papers, with analysis of failures caused by wrong method selection and insufficient compute.
claim_boundary: Surpassing a paper-specific metric is not the same as producing a journal-ready article.

name: ASI-Bench
evidence_note: Sixty project-level tasks across eleven domains. Progressive removal of procedures and methods makes human specification an explicit experimental variable.
claim_boundary: The benchmark prices neither academic guidance nor journal-ready output, which are the Portsmouth extensions.

name: AutoResearchEval
evidence_note: One hundred frontier-research tasks across seven domains, 800 trajectories and a 45-pattern failure taxonomy, emphasising weak evidence checking and path reconsideration.
claim_boundary: Trajectory quality is measured, but no institutional cost-per-output model is supplied.

name: AI Research Preference Models
evidence_note: Ranks unexecuted research candidates, with an agentic variant running cheap pilots before committing the main execution budget.
claim_boundary: Demonstrated on one machine-learning benchmark and scaffold; transfer to social science and journal-output cost is untested.

name: Science Sandboxes
evidence_note: A repeated experiment-feedback framework that distinguishes improving a metric from inferring the hidden rules that generate results.
claim_boundary: The paper instantiates biological and invented worlds; a business and management sandbox remains to be built.

name: Closing the Loop in AI-Driven Biomedical Discovery
evidence_note: A conceptual architecture for multi-loop discovery under sparse, delayed, noisy and costly verification, with explicit campaign state and human oversight.
claim_boundary: A non-peer-reviewed biomedical review; it provides an architecture rather than an evaluated social-science system.

name: ORAgentBench
evidence_note: A 107-task executable operations-research benchmark with hidden validators for schema, feasibility and objective quality.
claim_boundary: Tests optimisation work products, not complete management-science manuscripts.

name: Agents' Last Exam
evidence_note: A living benchmark of more than 1,000 long-horizon economically valuable tasks across 55 subfields and 13 industry clusters.
claim_boundary: Professional-task pass rates do not directly identify substitution within academic research production.

name: Qworld
evidence_note: Builds question-specific evaluation criteria through recursive expansion, offering a route from generic rubrics to article- and journal-specific review packs.
claim_boundary: LLM-generated criteria require human calibration before they can represent a journal-quality floor.

name: S-Researcher
evidence_note: A platform for simulation-based social inquiry, including large populations of simulated agents and inductive, deductive and abductive research modes.
claim_boundary: Simulation-based inquiry is one production mode and does not represent the observed Portsmouth journal portfolio.

name: AI Scientists Produce Results Without Reasoning Scientifically
evidence_note: Large-scale trace analysis showing that outcome scores can conceal ignored evidence and weak refutation-driven revision.
claim_boundary: Reasoning traces are imperfect evidence of internal reasoning; the study still provides a useful process audit.

name: Arbor: Hypothesis-Tree Research
evidence_note: A long-lived coordinator and executor architecture organised around a hypothesis tree linking claims, artefacts and evidence across research runs.
claim_boundary: Evidence spans a small set of research tasks and does not yet provide a costed university production function.

name: The Verification Gap in AI-Generated Research
evidence_note: A coded review of AI-research systems that distinguishes executable artefacts from harder-to-verify claims, reasoning traces and novelty.
claim_boundary: A survey of reported practices, not an independent audit of every system or benchmark.
